麻.meaning: An old sailor keeps a whole <part>grove</part> growing inside his garden <part>shed</part>, but the 'trees' are tall green stalks he strips every autumn and twists into ship's rope. His rope is so tough that a whale once used it to skip and couldn't snap it. It's all <kanji>hemp</kanji>.
麻.on: He drinks his tea from a big <sound>mu</sound>g wound round with rough rope.
麻.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' he sighs, sitting down on a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin to rest after a morning of twisting.

歴.meaning: Under a tall <part>cliff</part>, a forest school teaches its lessons in a <part>grove</part>: lesson one at the first tree, lesson two at the next, a few steps deeper each year. At the far end a <part>stop</part> sign marks graduation. Every pupil walks the same path: that's the <kanji>curriculum</kanji>.
歴.on: At the stop sign, each graduate is handed a <sound>re</sound>d <sound>ki</sound>wi to carry back up the cliff.

衆.meaning: A vampire opens a juice bar and pours one <part>blood</part> orange smoothie. Word spreads, and the queue winds out the door, round the block and over the hill. To stop pushing, he ties everyone to one long <part>thread</part>. He's serving the <kanji>masses</kanji>.
衆.on: One customer loses a <sound>shoe</sound> in the crush and hops the rest of the way to the counter.
衆.kun: '<sound>Ohh</sound>, so many!' gasps the vampire, staring at the endless line.

株.meaning: A banker keeps a <part>tree</part> on her desk and paints a <part>vermilion</part> stripe higher up its trunk each time her savings grow. When the paint nears the top, she sells one branch to her neighbour for a fortune, and he sells a twig to his. She trades in <kanji>stocks</kanji>.
株.on: She sweetens every deal with a cube of <sound>su</sound>gar for the buyer.
株.kun: When prices crash she stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, and feeds the tree's leaves to a <sound>bu</sound>ll under her desk.

尽.meaning: At the polar cafe, a penguin waddles the length of the counter to <part>measure</part> what's left of the stock: two lonely chips of <part>ice</part>. The walrus regulars slurped the rest all summer. Between them they've managed to <kanji>exhaust</kanji> a whole iceberg.
尽.on: The penguin offers hot <sound>gin</sound>ger tea instead, and the walruses groan.
尽.kun: The penguin lets out a chilly sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and turns the sign on the door to closed.

尊.meaning: Grandpa once cleared a blocked mountain pass with one stick of <part>lit dynamite</part> and a single swing of his <part>golf club</part>, chipping it neatly into the perfect crack. Now the whole valley bows when he shuffles by, and the club hangs in the town hall. He is deeply <kanji>revered</kanji>.
尊.on: Admirers line up to hang a fresh <sound>som</sound>brero on his statue every morning.
尊.kun: '<sound>Tut</sound>,' he clicks at anyone who doesn't bow, and the club rests on <sound>to</sound>p of a velvet cushion.

敬.meaning: At the circus, a curled <part>hedgehog</part> balances on the tip of a spinning folding <part>fan</part>, uncurls, and backflips onto the ringmaster's hat. The tent goes silent, every mouth hanging open. Then the whispers start. Everyone is in <kanji>awe</kanji>.
敬.on: Afterwards the ringmaster carries out a <sound>ca</sound>ke with one candle just for her.
敬.kun: Fans toss gifts into the ring to honour her: a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn, and a card signed 'from <sound>Ma</sound>'.

臼.meaning: A bear finds a heavy stone bowl in the woods, split down the middle into two halves with ridges inside, and decides it's a bath. He sits in it and the ridges scratch his back nicely. Then a squirrel climbs on, drops acorns on his belly and pounds them into flour. It was a <kanji>mortar</kanji> all along.
臼.on: The squirrel does the pounding with a pool <sound>cue</sound>, held upside down.
臼.kun: Soon the bear is grinding flour for <sound>u</sound>don noodles, then rice for <sound>su</sound>shi.

興.meaning: A busker builds a tiny theatre: a <part>frame</part> for the stage, a plank of <part>one</part> board inside, and a singing <part>mouth</part> puppet on top. On each side, half a <part>mortar</part> booms like a drum, and the whole thing stands on two legs splayed like an <part>eight</part>. Kids flock to it. He knows how to <kanji>entertain</kanji>.
興.on: The ticket price is one ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne per show.
興.kun: The drums even wake a sleepy <sound>o</sound>ctopus and a <sound>ko</sound>ala, who sit up to watch.

熟.meaning: Kids playing a <part>ball game</part> in the yard knock their ball, a hard green peach, onto a grill of <part>hot coals</part>. By the time they fish it out it's gone soft, golden and sweet, and so has everyone's mood: nobody remembers the score. Everything turns <kanji>mellow</kanji>.
熟.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of crows tastes the peach and gives full marks, while a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo dozes in the warm smoke.
熟.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>,' sigh the kids, as the peach splits open, perfectly ripe.

吹.meaning: A tired dragon is asked to light the birthday candles, but instead of fire its <part>mouth</part> lets out a giant <part>yawn</part>. The gust sends the candles, the cake and three guests sailing over the hedge. All it meant to do was gently <kanji>blow</kanji>.
吹.on: The guests land head first in a giant <sound>swee</sound>t jar next door, sticky but happy.
吹.kun: The birthday girl lands softly on a <sound>fu</sound>ton airing in the next garden.

闘.meaning: Behind the castle <part>gate</part>, two knights settle a quarrel in their own way: one hurls <part>beans</part> from a sack, the other swats every bean straight back with a <part>golf club</part>. The crowd cheers each swing and ducks each bean. It's the strangest <kanji>fight</kanji> the castle has ever seen.
闘.on: A stray bean lands right on the king's big <sound>toe</sound>.
闘.kun: Out of beans, the losing knight throws a <sound>ta</sound>co, another <sound>ta</sound>co, then a whole <sound>ca</sound>rp over the gate.

監.meaning: At the palace pool, a stern <part>servant</part> stands on the <part>diving board</part> with <part>two</part> whistles, watching everyone splash below. Anyone caught sneaking a snack must tip it into a <part>dish</part> by the steps. Nobody dares misbehave with her there to <kanji>oversee</kanji> it all.
監.on: She wears a pink <sound>car</sound>nation pinned to her swimsuit like a badge.

銃.meaning: A rich pirate refuses to use cannonballs. He has his blacksmith <part>fill</part> a long brass tube with <part>gold</part> coins, aims it at a rival ship and fires a glittering shower of treasure. The rival crew drops their swords to pick it up. It's the friendliest <kanji>gun</kanji> at sea.
銃.on: One of the coins is a big <sound>jew</sound>el, which knocks off the rival captain's hat.
銃.kun: The smoke makes the pirate sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!', as he peers down the barrel: a tube.

虚.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> floats out of his spaceship carrying a stand of <part>candles</part>, hoping to find a cosy corner of space. He strikes match after match, but nothing lights, nothing echoes, nothing is there at all. Just the endless black <kanji>void</kanji>.
虚.on: Far off, a tiny <sound>kio</sound>sk drifts by, shutters down.
虚.kun: A lonely <sound>moo</sound>se floats past, licking the last crumb of <sound>na</sound>an from an empty plate.

劣.meaning: At the beach weightlifting contest, the champion crab flexes a thousand ripples, while little Gary can show only a <part>few</part> specks of <part>muscle</part>. He lifts a single grain of sand, sighs, and hides in his shell with a deep feeling of <kanji>inferiority</kanji>.
劣.on: That night he sips a thimble of <sound>rets</sound>ina and tells the moon about it.
劣.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound> well,' he mumbles, and climbs a driftwood <sound>to</sound>tem pole to feel a bit taller.

巨.meaning: You open your bedside <part>drawer</part> to grab a sock and keep pulling. It slides out across the bedroom, through the wall and halfway down the street, with a whale snoring inside next to your socks. This drawer is <kanji>gigantic</kanji>.
巨.on: Further in, past the whale, there's a whole newspaper <sound>kio</sound>sk selling maps of the drawer.

偽.meaning: A con man keeps a disguise on every <part>coat hook</part> in his hall: a pilot's cap, a doctor's coat, a duchess's tiara. Each morning he picks one and writes his list of things to <part>do</part>: fly a plane, cure a cold, open a ball. Every line on it is a <kanji>falsehood</kanji>.
偽.on: Even his fancy watch is fake: every <sound>gear</sound> inside is painted on.
偽.kun: When he's caught, he squeaks '<sound>Ee</sound>!', fakes a sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and wails '<sound>Wah</sound>!' as if he were the victim.

崩.meaning: One night the <part>twin moons</part> hang too low and rest their chins on top of a <part>mountain</part> to gaze at the sea. They're heavier than they look: the peak creaks, cracks and slides away in a roaring river of pebbles. Even mountains <kanji>crumble</kanji>.
崩.on: Rangers spray down the dust with a long garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
崩.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo flees the rubble, clutching a yu<sound>zu</sound> in its beak.

壊.meaning: A giant wants a bigger house, so he gets rid of his old empty hut his own way: he heaps <part>soil</part> on it, throws a <part>net</part> over the top, stuffs an old <part>garment</part> down the chimney, counts to <part>ten</part> and stomps. Splinters fly everywhere. A one-giant <kanji>demolition</kanji>.
壊.on: The roof sails off into the sky like a <sound>ki</sound>te.
壊.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala napping in the rafters lands in the rubble and wails '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

唱.meaning: On a planet with a double <part>sun</part>, one disc stacked above the other, a choir of frogs opens every <part>mouth</part> at dawn and drones the same three words over and over until both suns are up. At sunset they start again. Their <kanji>chant</kanji> never changes.
唱.on: Tourists buy tickets: it's the best <sound>show</sound> in the swamp.
唱.kun: The lead frog sits on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, waving a piece of <sound>na</sound>an like a baton.

狭.meaning: Five anglers squeeze into a one-person ice-fishing tent. There's only room to dangle one <part>fishhook</part> through the hole, so the rest stand in a tight <part>group hug</part>, elbows in ears, rods up noses. It's very <kanji>cramped</kanji>.
狭.on: They pass the time dreaming aloud of a roomy holiday in <sound>Kyo</sound>to.
狭.kun: One angler tries to <sound>se</sound>ttle onto a stool, but it turns out to be his <sound>Ma</sound>'s knee.

偏.meaning: The school <part>notice board</part> is meant to be fair, but the caretaker only pins up his own daughter's drawings, and hangs his coat on the <part>coat hook</part> right over everyone else's posters. Nobody else's work gets seen. He's terribly <kanji>partial</kanji>.
偏.on: Even the prize for best drawing goes to his pet <sound>hen</sound>.
偏.kun: The hen sits <sound>ca</sound>lmly on a <sound>ta</sound>co, leaning to one side, pecking <sound>yo</sound>gurt from his spoon.

依.meaning: A wobbly old <part>coat hook</part> is barely screwed into the wall. The only thing holding it up is the heavy wool <part>garment</part> hanging on it, pressed flat against the plaster. If anyone takes that coat, the hook drops. It's completely <kanji>reliant</kanji> on it.
依.on: Inside the coat's pocket lives an <sound>ee</sound>l, who helps by curling its tail round the hook.
依.kun: The eel depends on the spoonfuls of <sound>yo</sound>gurt the owner leaves in the pocket each night.

恵.meaning: Every night a stranger sneaks out and plants <part>one</part> row of seedlings in a widow's empty <part>rice field</part>, then draws a little <part>heart</part> in the mud. By harvest the whole field is green, and nobody has seen who did it. It's a secret <kanji>favor</kanji>.
恵.on: On harvest day she leaves a <sound>ca</sound>ke on the fence post to say thank you.
恵.kun: Next morning the cake is gone, and in its place sits a <sound>me</sound>lon with a note: '<sound>Goo</sound>d luck.'

扱.meaning: A dockworker never lifts a crate by hand. She hooks each one with an <part>anchor</part> and swings it gently into a <part>catch net</part>, not a scratch on it. Eggs, pianos, a sleeping baby elephant: she knows how to <kanji>handle</kanji> anything.
扱.on: Even a slippery bar of <sound>soa</sound>p can't wriggle out of her net.
扱.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>... <sound>tsu</sound>!' she sneezes, and still catches a flying <sound>ca</sound>rp in the net.

拝.meaning: Shipwrecked on a bare island, a sailor drives his <part>anchor</part> into the sand beside the <part>one</part> thing that grows there: a single <part>corn stalk</part>. Every morning he kneels in front of it and thanks it for breakfast. He's begun to <kanji>worship</kanji> it.
拝.on: Bees build a <sound>hi</sound>ve in its leaves, and they bow to it too.
拝.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, great corn,' he prays, and offers it a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

償.meaning: At the fair, a clumsy juggler knocks over the pie stall. To make up for it, he hangs his own gold <part>prize</part> ribbon on the baker's <part>coat hook</part> and runs the stall for a whole week. The baker accepts it as <kanji>reparation</kanji>.
償.on: He even juggles pies in a free <sound>show</sound> to bring the customers back.
償.kun: The flour makes him sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', but he bakes her a <sound>goo</sound>d batch of <sound>na</sound>an to pay her back.

六.meaning: A beetle with just two legs, splayed like an <part>eight</part>, balances a jam-jar <part>lid</part> on its back and keeps toppling over. Each time, a friend glues on another pair of legs. By dinner it scuttles off happily with the right number for a bug: <kanji>six</kanji>.
六.on: Now it's so fast it rides a <sound>rock</sound>et round the garden.
六.kun: A cow counts the legs and lows '<sound>Moo</sound>', hiccups, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' Six exactly.

隔.meaning: A witch's <part>cauldron</part> keeps bubbling out a stinky green fog, so the villagers row it to a faraway rock and plant a warning <part>pennant</part> beside it. Only seagulls visit now, holding their beaks. They've managed to <kanji>isolate</kanji> it.
隔.on: The only thing beside it is a fish <sound>carc</sound>ass the gulls picked clean.
隔.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n guards the strip of sea between, and each time a boat turns back she clucks 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!'
